Senses.Explanation: The doubled cry of the Chan records: blue sky, blue sky — the exclamation of last resort when dismay, wonder, or the refusal to explain takes the voice. Zhaozhou Congshen answers a newcomer's plea for direction with the doubled cry alone, Pu'an Yinsu opens his own praise-verse with it — awakened to the birthless, talking without speaking of Chan, the two opened skin-flaps sweeping earth and heaven — Hanyue Fazang laments the painted-eye lacquer buckets racing from Tiantai and Nanyue to Hebei and Jiangnan, the mess not stopping in the eastern lands and the tangle beginning in the western heavens, and Tianyin Yuanxiu echoes his questioner's cry straight back, then verses that heaven has no cover and earth no bearer, the ten thousand images nowhere absent, the east village drinking and the west village dancing with no one to name as ruler. Muchen Daomin grants the failing monk his thirty blows to carry out and answers the plea to name where he went wrong with the doubled cry alone, Liangting Jingting finds the five-colored life-threads of the river festival a bewilderment with the cry itself added grief, Zishui wheels his whisk into nine circle-marks before any ancient buddha's birth and dares the hall to see — blue sky, blue sky — and Jifei Ruyi, praising the seventeenth ancestor who waited half a year with half his nostril gone and flew the father's shame abroad at a high price, rules that whether for the sparse or the dense it comes back to the same cry.
